North East Lincolnshire's population decreased by around 2,600 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

North East Lincolnshire's population decreased

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of North East Lincolnshire fell by 1.7%, from around 159,600 in 2011 to around 157,000 in 2021.

This means North East Lincolnshire was one of only three local authority areas in Yorkshire and The Humber to see its population decline. The regional population increased by 3.7%, while the population of England increased by 6.6%.

In 2021, North East Lincolnshire was home to around 5.8 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 5.9 in 2011. This area was close to the median population density across English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

The population of North East Lincolnshire decreased by around 1.7%

An older North East Lincolnshire

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of North East Lincolnshire increased by two years, from 41 to 43 years of age.

This area had a higher average (median) age than Yorkshire and The Humber as a whole in 2021 (40 years) and a higher average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 65 to 74 years rose by around 2,900 (an increase of 19.5%), while the number of residents between 35 and 49 years fell by just under 5,700 (17.2% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 65 and 74 years increased by 2.0 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Change in unpaid care

North East Lincolnshire saw England's joint second-largest percentage-point rise (alongside Blackpool, East Lindsey and Great Yarmouth) in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing between 20 and 49 hours of weekly unpaid care (from 1.4% in 2011 to 2.2% in 2021). These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

England's largest increase in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing between 20 and 49 hours of weekly unpaid care occurred in Hartlepool (from 1.8% to 2.9%).

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of those providing between 20 and 49 hours of weekly unpaid care in North East Lincolnshire increased by 0.8 percentage points

Fall in unemployment

North East Lincolnshire saw Yorkshire and The Humber's second-largest percentage-point fall in the proportion of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were unemployed (from 5.8% in 2011 to 2.8% in 2021).

Across the region, only Kingston upon Hull saw a greater fall in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were unemployed (from 7.4% to 4.1%).

Every local authority area across Yorkshire and The Humber saw a fall in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were unemployed, as the regional percentage fell from 4.4% to 2.7%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were unemployed (excluding full-time students) in North East Lincolnshire decreased by 3.0 percentage points

Change in work hours

In 2021, 11.8% of North East Lincolnshire residents aged 16 years and over and in employment said they worked over 49 hours per week. This figure decreased from 12.8% in 2011.

The decrease in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked over 49 hours per week was greater across Yorkshire and The Humber (2.0 percentage points, from 11.9% to 9.9%) than in North East Lincolnshire (1.0 percentage points). Across England, the percentage fell by 2.2 percentage points, from 13.3% to 11.1%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults in employment who worked 49 hours or more in North East Lincolnshire decreased by 1.0 percentage points

Disability in North East Lincolnshire

In 2021, 9.0% of North East Lincolnshire residents were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. This figure decreased from 9.7% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, around one in nine people (11.1%) were identified as being disabled and limited a little, compared with 10.7% in 2011. The proportion of North East Lincolnshire residents who were not disabled increased from 79.6% to 79.9%.

The decrease in the proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot was greater across Yorkshire and The Humber (1.7 percentage points, from 9.9% to 8.2%) than in North East Lincolnshire (0.7 percentage points). Across England, the proportion fell by 1.6 percentage points, from 9.1% to 7.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in North East Lincolnshire decreased by 0.7 percentage points

Rise in private renting

Of North East Lincolnshire households, 22.4% rented privately in 2021, up from 18.1% in 2011.

In 2021, just over one in eight households (13.2%) lived in socially rented housing, compared with 14.5% in 2011. The percentage of North East Lincolnshire households that owned their home (outright or with a mortgage or loan) decreased from 66.1% to 63.9%.

The increase in the percentage of privately-rented homes was greater in North East Lincolnshire (4.3 percentage points) than across Yorkshire and The Humber (3.5 percentage points, from 15.9% to 19.4%). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.6 percentage points, from 16.8% to 20.5%.

Private renting in North East Lincolnshire increased by 4.3 percentage points

Religion in North East Lincolnshire

In 2021, 46.5% of North East Lincolnshire residents reported having "No religion", making it the most common response in this local authority area (up from 30.4% in 2011). Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across Yorkshire and The Humber, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 25.9% to 39.4%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 45.3% of people in North East Lincolnshire described themselves as Christian (down from 60.7%), while 5.9% did not state their religion (down from 7.2% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

In 2021, 46.5% of usual residents in North East Lincolnshire reported having "No religion"

North East Lincolnshire residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 144,100 North East Lincolnshire residents said they were born in England. This represented 91.8% of the local population. The figure has decreased from around 149,600 in 2011, which at the time represented 93.7% of North East Lincolnshire's population.

Poland was the next most represented, with just over 1,800 North East Lincolnshire residents reporting this country of birth (1.2%). This figure was up from around 1,200 in 2011, which at the time represented 0.8% of the population of North East Lincolnshire.

The number of North East Lincolnshire residents born in Scotland fell from just under 2,000 in 2011 (1.2% of the local population) to around 1,600 in 2021 (1.0%).

In 2021, 91.8% of North East Lincolnshire residents reported their country of birth as England

Health in North East Lincolnshire

In 2021, 43.1% of North East Lincolnshire residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 42.6% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 35.6% to 35.4%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of North East Lincolnshire residents describing their health as "very bad" remained 1.4%, while those describing their health as "bad" remained 4.9%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in very good health in North East Lincolnshire increased by 0.5 percentage points

Family in North East Lincolnshire

Of North East Lincolnshire households, 17.5% included a couple but no children in 2021, down from 18.1% in 2011.

In 2021, just under one in six households (16.4%) included a couple with dependent children, compared with 17.8% in 2011. The percentage of single family households including a couple living with only non-dependent children decreased from 6.3% to 6.2%.

The decrease in the percentage of households including a couple but no children was greater across Yorkshire and The Humber (1.0 percentage points, from 18.7% to 17.7%) than in North East Lincolnshire (0.5 percentage points). Across England, the percentage fell by 0.9 percentage points, from 17.6% to 16.8%.

The percentage of households including a couple without children in North East Lincolnshire decreased by 0.5 percentage points

National identity in North East Lincolnshire

In 2021, 4.1% of North East Lincolnshire residents did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK. This figure increased from 2.5% in 2011.

In 2021, 0.6% of residents identified with a UK and non-UK national identity, compared with 0.2% in 2011. The percentage of residents in North East Lincolnshire that identified as "British only" increased from 11.8% to 55.3%.

The increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK in North East Lincolnshire (1.6 percentage points) was similar to the increase across Yorkshire and The Humber (1.6 percentage points, from 5.1% to 6.7%). Across England, the percentage increased by 1.7 percentage points, from 8.2% to 10.0%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in North East Lincolnshire increased by 1.6 percentage points

More adults never married or in a civil partnership

Of North East Lincolnshire residents aged 16 years and over, 36.2% said they had never been married or in a civil partnership in 2021, up from 33.1% in 2011.

In 2021, just over 4 in 10 people (42.8%) said they were married or in a registered civil partnership, compared with 45.3% in 2011. The percentage of adults in North East Lincolnshire that had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership remained at 11.2%.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership was greater across Yorkshire and The Humber (3.8 percentage points, from 33.9% to 37.7%) than in North East Lincolnshire (3.1 percentage points). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.3 percentage points, from 34.6% to 37.9%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in North East Lincolnshire increased by 3.1 percentage points

Ethnic groups in North East Lincolnshire

In 2021, 0.7% of North East Lincolnshire residents identified their ethnic group within the "Other" category ("Arab" or "Any other ethnic group"), up from 0.3% in 2011. The 0.4 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across Yorkshire and The Humber, the percentage of people from the "Other ethnic groups" ("Arab" or "Any other ethnic group") increased from 0.8% to 1.4%, while across England the percentage increased from 1.0% to 2.2%.

In 2021, 96.2% of people in North East Lincolnshire identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 97.4% in 2011), while 1.6% identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category (compared with 1.3% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category increased from 0.7% in 2011 to 1.0% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.
